title: The Palace of King David: Excavations at the Summit of the City of David, Preliminary Report of Seasons 2005-2007
author: Eilat Mazar
publisher: Shoham Academic Research and Publication, Jerusalem
allowedUseNotes: Copyrighted excavation report. Project stores its own summary of the excavator's argument and dating only; no reproduction of plans, photographs, or the report's text.
summary: Eilat Mazar's preliminary excavation report on the 'Large Stone Structure' she uncovered at the summit of the City of David (first announced in a 2005 dig season and popularized in Mazar, 'Did I Find King David's Palace?', Biblical Archaeology Review 32/1 [2006]). Mazar reads a complex of massive walls built of large, roughly hewn stones as belonging to a single monumental public building, dates it to the 11th-10th centuries BCE on the basis of associated pottery, and proposes identifying it with David's palace (2 Samuel 5:11). She reads the adjoining 'Stepped Stone Structure' -- a massive stone-and-earth terrace system descending the City of David's steep northeastern slope -- as a supporting substructure for the building above it, and as a candidate for the biblical Millo (2 Samuel 5:9's 'from the Millo inward'). This project cites Mazar's excavation and dating as the primary, named source for the 'more substantial administrative center' pole of the tenth-century Jerusalem extent dispute (claim-jebusite-stronghold-form) and as one of two named sources (with naaman-2014-davids-palace-millo) behind the terrace/stepped-structure identification proposal for the Millo (claim-millo-identification). Both the single-building interpretation and the tenth-century dating have been directly disputed in the peer-reviewed literature -- see finkelstein-herzog-singer-avitz-ussishkin-2007-tel-aviv, cited on the same claim for the opposing reading -- and this project adopts neither position as settled.
confidenceNotes: Bibliographic details (publisher, 2009, ~100pp preliminary report; the earlier 2006 BAR 32/1 popular announcement) are drawn from multiple independent secondary web citations (publisher/bookseller listings, academic reviews, and citing bibliographies) that agree with each other, not from direct inspection of the report itself. TO VERIFY: exact page range of the 2006 BAR article and specific stratigraphic/pottery dating arguments within the 2009 report against a primary copy. The single-building interpretation and the proposed date are both contested by other excavators (see finkelstein-herzog-singer-avitz-ussishkin-2007-tel-aviv); this project treats Mazar's reading as one named pole of a live dispute, not as an established finding.
